\section[geloso]{geloso — jealous}

\label{lesson:IT-C218-geloso}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for certainly, then the Italian for really.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: geloso}
\textbf{geloso} — \textquotedblleft{}jealous\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{geloso} $\leftarrow$ Old Provençal \emph{gelos} — borrowed, a word of the troubadours; behind it is Late Latin \emph{zelosus}, \textquotedblleft{}full of zeal\textquotedblright{}. (EtymDB 2.1 records the Latin word, but calls the Italian inherited.)
\end{cousinweb}
